# make new repository 
# make new project 
# make new document r markdown 

```{r}
library(tidyverse) 
library(ggridges)
library(p8105.datasets)
data("weather_df")

```

Lets make a scatterplot 
```{r}
ggplot(weather_df, aes(x = tmin, y = tmax))+
  geom_point()
```

```{r}
ggp_temp_scatterplot = 
weather_df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = tmin, y = tmax)) +
  geom_point(aes(color=name),alpha = 0.25 ) + 
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE)
             

ggp_temp_scatterplot
```

show faceting 
```{r}
weather_df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = tmin, y = tmax, color= name)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5 ) + 
  facet_grid(. ~name) # column , old
```

```{r}
weather_df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = tmin, y = tmax, color= name)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5 ) + 
  facet_grid(cols = vars(name)) # new 
```

```{r}

weather_df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = date, y= tmax, color = name)) + 
  geom_point(aes(size = prcp),alpha = 0.5) + 
  facet_grid(. ~name)

```

make a plot of central park tmax v tmin onlu, convert temperatures to F

```{r}

weather_df |> 
  filter(name == "CentralPark_NY") |>
  mutate(
    tmax = tmax *(9/5) + 32,
    tmin = tmin *(9/5) + 32
  )|>
  ggplot(aes(x = tmin, y= tmax)) + 
  geom_point()


```

What is a hex plot 

```{r}
weather_df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x=tmin, y=tmax))+ 
  geom_hex()
```

## univariate plots 

```{r}
weather_df |>
  ggplot(aes(x =tmax, fill = name)) + 
  geom_histogram() +
facet_grid(. ~name)

```


density plots 

```{r}
weather_df |>
  ggplot(aes(x= tmax, fill = name)) + 
  geom_density (alpha = 0.3)
```

boxplots 
```{r}
weather_df |> 
  
  ggplot(aes(x = name,y= tmax)) + 
  geom_boxplot()

```

violin plot

```{r}
weather_df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x= name, y = tmax)) + 
  geom_violin() 

```


ridge plots
```{r}
weather_df |> 
  ggplot ( aes( x = tmax, y = name)) + 
  geom_density_ridges()
```

## save some of my plots 

```{r}
  ggp_weather= 
  weather_df |> 

  ggplot( aes( x = date, y =tmax, color = name)) + 
  geom_point(aes(size = prcp), alpha = 0.5) + 
  facet_grid(. ~name) 

ggp_weather

ggsave("images/ggp_wether.pdf", ggp_weather)
```
